When your argument—or in this case, a photograph—contradicts common and therefore often limited assumptions about a complex subject, the lack of hard evidence can indeed make it difficult to support your position, especially when the prevailing opinions are based on hearsay or small selection of widely known artifacts.
Yet in such situations, our best resource remains the judgment of experts.
Scholars have identified the photograph in question as Vaslav Nijinsky portraying the "Negro" in the ballet _Le Roi Candaule_, no later than 1907.
This attribution is supported by multiple publications.

To reconcile own fixed opinion with information that feels difficult to accept, one must remember that Nijinsky was an artist of extraordinary range _—_ a metamorph, capable of profound and convincing transformation.
To expand the boundaries of this myth—which inevitably narrows our understanding of the past—we must remain open to learning more.
The scattered bits of information that is there can help us reconcile images that may, at first glance, seem impossible to align.
The bottom line: the identity of Vaslav Nijinsky in the photo is definite, the ballet and the role are debatable.
